page: Microsoft Azure B2ats_v2 is a burstable virtual machine belonging to the Basv2 family. It is powered by an AMD EPYC 7763 processor utilizing the x86_64 architecture. The server features 2 vCPUs mapped to 1 physical core with 2 threads, operating at a clock speed of 3.525 GHz. It is configured with 1.0 GB of system memory, yielding a low memory-to-core ratio of 0.5 GB per core. There is no local storage bundled with this instance, though it is premium storage capable, and it does not include any GPUs or complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark data highlights a stark contrast between single-core and multi-core capabilities. The stress-ng single-core CPU performance is strong, placing in the top 25% with a score of 2701.19. However, the multi-core CPU performance is weak, scoring identically at 2701.19 and placing in the bottom 25%. Memory performance is highly constrained, with a cached small-block read-only memory bandwidth of 140.76 GB/sec and a PassMark memory score of 0.0, both falling into the bottom 10%. PassMark CPU tests show weak overall performance of 3130.58 and poor physics simulation results of 391.83. Redis SET operations reach 2.25 million operations per second, and static web serving throughput is measured at 2.77 GB/sec.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the B2ats_v2 offers a highly economical entry point for workloads that do not require continuous CPU utilization or large memory footprints. The burstable CPU allocation model allows the instance to handle brief spikes in demand while maintaining a low baseline resource cost. Due to the tiny 1.0 GB memory capacity and weak multi-core and database benchmark results, this server is not suitable for memory-intensive applications, databases, or heavy multi-threaded processing. It is best suited for lightweight, bursty workloads such as low-traffic static web serving, simple microservices, basic scripting, or development and testing environments.
